title: American/British English Accent Detection
description:
Project Overview:I am currently developing a Python-based project focused on the detection of accents, with a particular emphasis on distinguishing between American and British accents. This project aims to analyze two types of audio samples: one that exhibits a flawless American accent, which could be either AI-generated or uttered by a native speaker, and another that is recorded by a user. The system is designed to assess how closely the user's accent matches the standard American or British accent they select, specifically in terms of pronunciation accuracy. This assessment is anticipated to be represented as a percentage, indicating the level of similarity.Additionally, I am eager to deepen my understanding of the entire coding and development process behind this project. I am looking forward to learning directly under your guidance, either by working together or through side-by-side instruction in regular meetings. My goal is to thoroughly comprehend every aspect of the project. I am committed to coding alongside you on a regular basis, and I am ready to dedicate as much time as necessary to build this project together, given that there is no strict deadline.Project Requirements:Accent Detection Model: At the heart of this project is the need for a pre-trained model or the development of a new model that is capable of analyzing audio samples for the purpose of accent comparison. This model must be adept at identifying discrepancies in pronunciation and quantifying the similarities in accents.Model Integration or Development: Although I have initiated some groundwork with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), I am open to the idea of integrating a model from Hugging Face or adopting any other advanced methodology you suggest. The main aim is to ensure that the model can effectively distinguish between accent similarities with a high degree of accuracy.Audio Comparison and Feedback System: The proposed system will allow users to select an American or British accent for comparison. Following this selection, a reference audio clip in the chosen accent will be played. Subsequently, users will be prompted to record their own attempt at mimicking the heard accent. Importantly, the GUI or the command-line interface will offer users the option to listen to their own recorded audio before initiating the comparison process. If they are not satisfied with their recording, they will have the opportunity to re-record themselves. Moreover, users will be able to listen to the AI-generated or native speaker's voice multiple times to ensure they are fully prepared. The model will then compare the user's audio against the reference, providing a similarity score. If the similarity score surpasses 90%, the user will be congratulated. Conversely, if the score falls below 90%, the system will examine the user's pronunciation, marking correctly pronounced words in green and incorrectly pronounced words in red.Interactive User Interface: The application may be equipped with either a Graphical User Interface (GUI) or a command-line interface, enabling users to:
- Choose between an American or British accent for analysis.
- Select sentences from a predefined list to mimic, thereby enriching the learning experience through diverse examples.
- Receive auditory cues for recording prompts, followed by immediate feedback on their pronunciation accuracy.
- Listen to their own recording before proceeding with the comparison, with an option to re-record if necessary.
- Repeatedly listen to the reference audio to better understand the target accent.Technical Specifications: This project entails the application of CNNs, the utilization of pre-trained models, or the creation of a bespoke model specifically designed for accent analysis. It is imperative that the system can efficiently conduct audio comparisons, offering users valuable feedback on their pronunciation proficiency in relation to the chosen accent.

title: Optimization and Deployment of AI News Analysis Web App
description: IntroductionWe have developed an AI News Analysis web app that leverages Python for its development. The application integrates Bing News and Search API, as well as the OpenAI API, to enhance user input queries. This issue hinders our ability to deploy our API on AWS Lambda functions.ObjectiveThe main goal is to rewrite the application code from scratch for optimization & enhancement, develop an API for the existing functions using FastAPI, and deploy the optimized application on AWS Lambda functions. This will ensure that the application is efficient, scalable, and meets the deployment requirements of AWS Lambda.Scope of Work1. Code Analysis• Objective: Study and understand the current codebase to extract the necessary logic and functionalities.• Tasks:• Review the existing web app's codebase.• Identify key functionalities, algorithms, and logic used in the application.• Document the core components and their interactions.2. Code Rewrite• Objective: Rewrite the application code from scratch using the documented logic and functionalities as a reference, ensuring optimization and efficiency.• Tasks:• Develop a clean, optimized codebase using Python, focusing on minimizing dependencies and removing unused libraries.• Ensure the new codebase adheres to best practices for scalability, maintainability, and performance.• Incorporate Bing News and Search API and OpenAI API integrations as per the existing logic.3. FastAPI Development• Objective: Develop a FastAPI-based API for all the application functions to facilitate easy integration and scalability.• Tasks:• Design and implement API endpoints for each functionality of the web app.• Ensure comprehensive API documentation for ease of use and integration.• Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms to secure API access.4. Deployment on AWS Lambda• Objective: Deploy the optimized application on AWS Lambda functions, ensuring that the deployment is efficient and the application is scalable.• Tasks:• Containerize the FastAPI application using Docker, ensuring the Docker image is optimized for size and performance.• Set up the AWS Lambda environment and configure it to host the Docker container.• Implement CI/CD pipelines for automated testing and deployment of the application.Deliverables• A fully rewritten and optimized codebase for the AI News Analysis web app.• A fully functional FastAPI API for the web app's functionalities.• Documentation covering the API endpoints, usage, and integration guide.• A deployed and functional version of the application on AWS Lambda.Project TimelineThe project is expected to be completed within TWO WEEKS, from the commencement date. A detailed timeline will be provided upon project initiation, outlining key milestones and deadlines.ConclusionThis project aims to significantly improve the performance, scalability, and deployment capabilities of the AI News Analysis web app. By rewriting the application code from scratch, developing a FastAPI API, and deploying the application on AWS Lambda, we aim to provide a robust solution that meets the immediate and future needs of our users.

- Detailed documentation and comments
- Readme with in depth description of project and how to run the project.This task is designed to provide you with a simple, clean Web API.Please read through this document carefully before starting.Development environmentMake sure you have the following products/accounts installed before beginning the challenge:• Visual Studio 2022 (Community edition is fine)https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/vs/community/• Microsoft SQL Server Expresshttps://www.microsoft.com/en-au/sql-server/sql-server-downloads• Microsoft SQL Server Management Studiohttps://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/ssms/download-sql-server-management-studio-ssms?view=sql-server-ver15• .Net 6 SDKhttps://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/6.0• A Github accountSetupBegin by cloning the repo – Will be providedDownload all required packages via the dotnet restore command.Build the project to ensure everything is working correctly.Work item 1 – Todos CRUDThe project you have downloaded is a barebones Web API, set up with dependency injection andEntity Framework. The database contains a single table (Todos).Examine the TodosController. You will see four endpoints ready to handle the CRUD operations ofthe Todos.Build out these endpoints using the ITodoService to declare the service methods the controller willcall, and then implement those methods in the TodoService class.Note: the view model/DTO TodoVM is currently empty. Make sure you build that out so that the APIonly deals with the TodoVM (let the service handle the domain models!)Ensure you include:1) Asynchronous handling of all CRUD operations2) Exception handling and loggingYou will know you’re finished when...You can start the project and hit each of the four endpoints using Postman, sending and receivingdata from your API.Work item 2 – Relational entitiesNow the API can handle CRUD methods for our Todos, we need to expand the project to includedifferent Todo lists for different users.Modify the product to add a new database table of Users, with each user record having a collectionof Todo items.Modify the API so the Http Get endpoint accepts a parameter of userID, returning only the Todoitems for that user. Ensure the remaining endpoints also handle the new user-todo relationship.

This testing phase encompasses rigorous checks to ensure that notifications are successfully sent and received as intended. Customize the payload structure to suit the specifications of each platform supported by the application (e.g., Android, Chrome).4. Conduct comprehensive testing to validate the functionality of the application post-migration.5. Address and resolve any issues or discrepancies discovered during testing to ensure seamless notification delivery.Links:Base Application: https://smartiolabs.com/product/smart-push-notification-systemGoogle Firebase Doc: https://firebase.google.com/docs/cloud-messagingFirebase Migration Doc: https://firebase.google.com/docs/cloud-messaging/migrate-v1Deliverables:1. Fully migrated PHP application seamlessly integrated with Firebase's HTTPv1 API.2. Detailed documentation outlining the changes made during the migration process, including instructions for future maintenance and updates.3. Comprehensive test results confirming the application's functionality across all supported platforms post-migration.Expectations:The ideal candidate will possess expertise in PHP development, with a strong understanding of API integrations and migration processes. They should demonstrate proficiency in working with Firebase APIs and be able to navigate the intricacies of transitioning from legacy systems to modern protocols. Effective communication throughout the migration process is crucial, as is the ability to deliver a fully functional application within the agreed-upon timeframe.This project offers an opportunity to contribute to the optimization and future-proofing of a critical application infrastructure, ensuring continued reliability and performance in delivering post notifications across various platforms.Please clarify the following questions:1. Can you discuss your experience with PHP development and working on custom-built applications?2. How would you approach updating the authentication mechanism in the PHP application to align with Firebase's HTTPv1 requirements?3. What testing methodologies do you typically employ to ensure the functionality and reliability of applications post-migration?4. What is your experience with Firebase APIs, and can you provide an example of how you've utilized them in previous projects?5. Can you provide an example of a challenge you encountered while working with Firebase APIs in a previous project and how you addressed it?These questions aim to evaluate the candidate's technical proficiency, problem-solving skills, and familiarity with Firebase, ensuring they are well-equipped to handle the requirements of the migration project effectively.Please Note: Apps using deprecated FCM legacy APIs for HTTP and XMPP must migrate to HTTP v1 API soon. Sending messages (including upstream messages) with these APIs was deprecated on June 20, 2023, and will be removed in June 2024.

This should include options for bulk uploads via xls or csv files with field mapping capabilities, or through an automated inventory reading mode using the system itself, making the process as efficient as possible.6. **Security, Privacy, and Documentation**: Implement top-tier security measures to safeguard retailer data and ensure compliance with privacy standards. Additionally, provide comprehensive documentation and support for system setup, use, and troubleshooting, including updates.#### Ideal Candidate(s):

title: Simple Tableau Data Analysis
description: ACME, home of the ACME Kleen Earth Office Shears, is a chain of stores with locations around the world. The dataset contained here includes orders, returns, and customer information.We will use these data for our Data Analytics exercises. The data (Excel) can be found in the attachment. You can register in Tableau for free. Register today as sometimes verification process might take longer than what is expected.Work instructionsCustomer Categorization: The concept began in B2B marketing long ago, and, like Relationship Marketing, has also been adopted by B2C marketing. This idea is simple and closely related to inventory management control. Customers come in three types, A, B and C.‘A’ customers are your most profitable. According to the Pareto Principle, 20% of your customers account for 80% of your profit. These customers deserve your attention and priority. Keep them coming back.‘C’ customers may not be profitable at all or account for very little profit. They’re probably not worth the effort put into them and can be dropped or dissuaded from returning. At the very least, ignore them.‘B’ customers are somewhere in the middle. The aggregate of their sales is large but their profitability is nowhere near ‘A’ customers. Can they be turned into ‘A’ customers? Are they worth that effort?If you’re interested in learning more about customer categorization and profit try this (optional) Harvard Business Review article:This job entails, you guessed it, categorizing Acme’s customers. Identify A, B, and C customers in your assigned Segment (each customer will belong to one of three “buckets”).Analyze the Corporate segment.Build a Story (in Tableau) to show the 3 groups and visually show their profitability (hint: this requires more than just a list of names, but make sure the names are there). (Hint: Tableau wants to cut off the list and you're going to have to do some manipulation to get the top 20 to show properly.) description: API : https://github.com/polygon-io/client-goTo ensure the accuracy and reliability of our system, it is crucial to manage system time effectively, particularly in addressing time drift. This entails continuous synchronization with an NTP (Network Time Protocol) server to maintain alignment with global time standards. Once we know the Timedrift and our latency we can also use timestamps of incoming data to align continuously as the timestamp will be based on the exchange which is very precise.For data acquisition, we leverage both the Polygon API (available via Go or RESTful interfaces). The process is initiated by specifying a target date, for example, [phone removed], to the Go program. Utilizing the API, the system retrieves all option contracts for "O:SPXW" (excluding "SPX" optiosn) expiring on the specified date, with strike prices within a 5% range above and below the current market value.Additionally, the API facilitates querying the last known index price for "I:SPX", providing a reference for market conditions to be able to get that 10% above or below.From the retrieved data, we expect to isolate approximately 100-150 contracts expiring on the given day. Subsequently, the system establishes a connection to the WebSocket for real-time data streaming or utilizes the Go API for the same purpose, encompassing all relevant contracts. utilizing both our system clock and time stamps from incoming data we can move forward in 500ms increments.We begin by aggregating data points every 500 milliseconds, starting at 9:30:00.000, capturing both the first quote and the initial index point of the trading session. It's important to note that we are dealing with real-time quotes, utilizing the last available quote closest to 9:29:59.9999 for our initial data point. Additionally, index data is published every second, allowing us to potentially use these timestamps to monitor and adjust for any clock drift, as they are issued precisely every second.An example of the data format we receive is as follows:"ask_exchange": 302,"ask_price": 9.8,"ask_size": 3,"bid_exchange": 302,"bid_price": 9.4,"bid_size": 1,"sequence_number": 303635,"sip_timestamp": [phone removed]For each of the 100+ contracts, we calculate the midpoint price by averaging the ask_price and bid_price. This value serves as our reference for further calculations. To determine the option's delta, we first need to compute the implied volatility (IV) using a fast bisection method. This calculated IV is then inputted into the Black-Scholes model to compute the delta for each option. I have an example wrote in GO for both of these as guidelines, but might need further optimization.After calculating IV / delta for all options, we organize them to identify those closest to a delta of 0.50 for calls and -0.50 for puts, which indicates options at or near the money.print the put and call option closest to closest abs to .50 delta to terminal showing latency
